title: Completeness of pure coface word relations within the endpoint degrees
statement: Let $\Delta$ be the category of nonempty finite ordinals $[r]=\{0<\cdots<r\}$ and nondecreasing maps [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For $r\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq r$, let $\delta_i^r:[r-1]\to[r]$ be the increasing injection omitting $i$. Fix integers $0\leq a\leq b$. A coface word from $[a]$ to $[b]$ is a finite composable sequence of these maps, including the empty word when $a=b$; its value is their composite, with composition read right to left. If two coface words from $[a]$ to $[b]$ have equal values as maps of ordered sets, one can transform one word into the other by finitely many replacements of adjacent subwords, in either direction, using only the typed relations $$\delta_j^{r+1}\circ\delta_i^r=\delta_i^{r+1}\circ\delta_{j-1}^r\qquad(r\geq1,\ 0\leq i<j\leq r+1).$$ All words and all replacements in the transformation involve only ordinals with degrees between $a$ and $b$; no codegeneracy or mixed relation is used.

proof.text: Put $k=b-a$. Reading a coface word from left to right (outermost map first), write it as $\delta_{j_1}^{b}\circ\delta_{j_2}^{b-1}\circ\cdots\circ\delta_{j_k}^{a+1}$, with $0\leq j_t\leq b-t+1$. Each coface raises the degree by one, so every word has exactly this length and these intermediate degrees. For $k=0$ the only word is empty. The definition of the cofaces gives $\delta_j^r(x)=x$ for $x<j$ and $x+1$ for $x\geq j$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set].

source.place: Tag 0168 (lemma-face-degeneracy-category), omitted pure-coface presentation proof, supplied here by Q46; Tag 0167 (lemma-relations-face-degeneracy), part (1)

proof.text: Whenever an adjacent pair has outer index $j$ and inner index $i<j$, replace $\delta_j^{r+1}\circ\delta_i^r$ by $\delta_i^{r+1}\circ\delta_{j-1}^r$. The replacement is typed: $i\leq r$ implies $i\leq r+1$, while $0\leq j-1\leq r$ follows from $1\leq j\leq r+1$. Here $r\geq a+1\geq1$ because two consecutive cofaces occur. The two maps have equal values by [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-face-identity], and composing on either side preserves that equality. The sum of all indices decreases by exactly one: $j+i$ becomes $i+(j-1)$.

source.place: Tag 0168 (lemma-face-degeneracy-category), omitted pure-coface presentation proof, supplied here by Q46; Tag 0167 (lemma-relations-face-degeneracy), part (1)

proof.text: Induct strongly on the nonnegative sum of the indices to obtain a finite sequence of these replacements ending in a word $N$ with $j_1\leq\cdots\leq j_k$. Indeed, if there is an adjacent decrease, step 2 gives a smaller sum and the induction hypothesis applies to that word; if there is none, the original word already has the required inequalities and needs zero replacements. The sum-zero case has only zero indices and hence no decrease. Every replacement keeps the degree sequence $a,a+1,\ldots,b$ and, by step 2, the value.

source.place: Tag 0168 (lemma-face-degeneracy-category), omitted pure-coface presentation proof, supplied here by Q46; Tag 0167 (lemma-relations-face-degeneracy), part (1)

proof.text: For such an ordered word $N$, its omitted vertices in $[b]$ are exactly $j_1,j_2+1,\ldots,j_k+k-1$, in strictly increasing order. Here is the induction on $k$: the empty word has empty complement; for $k>0$ write $N=\delta_{j_1}^b\circ T$. The tail $T$ is ordered and by induction has complement $\{j_2,j_3+1,\ldots,j_k+k-2\}$ in $[b-1]$. All these entries are at least $j_1$. The formula in step 1 shifts each of them by one under $\delta_{j_1}^b$, and the only vertex outside the image of this coface is $j_1$. Consequently $[b]\setminus\operatorname{im}(N)=\{j_1\}\cup\delta_{j_1}^b([b-1]\setminus\operatorname{im}(T))$, giving the claimed list. Its entries are strictly increasing since $j_t\leq j_{t+1}$; they lie in $[b]$ since $j_t+t-1\leq b$.

source.place: Tag 0168 (lemma-face-degeneracy-category), omitted pure-coface presentation proof, supplied here by Q46; Tag 0167 (lemma-relations-face-degeneracy), part (1)

proof.text: Two ordered words with the same value have the same omitted set. The increasing lists in step 4 therefore agree: their first entries are both the least element of that set; remove it and repeat for each following entry. Thus $j_t+t-1=j_t^{\prime}+t-1$ for every $t$, so $j_t=j_t^{\prime}$ and the words are identical. Apply step 3 to the two words in the statement. Their ordered endpoints have equal values by step 2, hence are identical by this argument. Follow the first finite reduction and then the reverse of the second. This is the required transformation using only the stated coface relations; the degree bound is preserved at each move. For $k=1$ no replacement is needed and equality of the omitted singleton determines the sole index.
